title: A coherent module whose support is a union of two closed subsets is an extension of modules supported on each
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme], i.e. locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let $\mathcal F$ be a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. For an $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal G$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] let $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal G)=\{x\in X:\mathcal G_x\ne0\}$ [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base](2), $\mathcal G_x$ the stalk [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. Suppose $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)=Z\cup Z'$ with $Z,Z'\subseteq X$ closed subsets. Then there is a coherent sub-$\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal G'\subseteq\mathcal F$ such that $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal G')\subseteq Z'$ and $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F/\mathcal G')\subseteq Z$, where $\mathcal F/\mathcal G'$ is the cokernel of the inclusion $\mathcal G'\to\mathcal F$ (a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module); that is, a short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal G'\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal G\to0$ of coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules with $\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal G'\subseteq Z'$ and $\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal G\subseteq Z$.

proof.text: Take the actual Mathlib vanishing ideal K of Z. Its support is Z. The quasi-coherent ideal zero-set theorem applied to its canonical closed subscheme identifies the proper-stalk locus with this support.

source.place: Tag 01YD, lemma-prepare-filter-support, proof: restriction of I^n F to X minus Z'; with Schemes Tag 01I8 and Modules Tag 01CE. Read online at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01YD.

proof.text: On the Noetherian open V = X minus Z', restrict F and K. Coherence restricts, restriction identifies stalks, and support_comap identifies the ideal support with its preimage. Thus the support of F restricted to V lies in the proper-stalk locus of K restricted to V. The ideal-power annihilation theorem supplies an exponent t.

source.place: Tag 01YD, lemma-prepare-filter-support, proof: restriction of I^n F to X minus Z'; with Schemes Tag 01I8 and Modules Tag 01CE. Read online at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01YD.

proof.text: The ideal-power restriction zero comparison shows that K^t F restricts to zero on V. Set G' = K^t F and take its canonical image inclusion i into F.

source.place: Tag 01YD, lemma-prepare-filter-support, proof: restriction of I^n F to X minus Z'; with Schemes Tag 01I8 and Modules Tag 01CE. Read online at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01YD.

proof.text: Coherence implies quasi-coherence on a locally Noetherian scheme. Every ideal power is quasi-coherent, including exponent zero (the unit sheaf). Its tensor product with F is quasi-coherent, and so is the image of multiplication. The coherent-submodule theorem gives coherence of G' and its cokernel.

source.place: Tag 01YD, lemma-prepare-filter-support, proof: restriction of I^n F to X minus Z'; with Schemes Tag 01I8 and Modules Tag 01CE. Read online at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01YD.

proof.text: The image inclusion is monic; the abelian cokernel sequence is short exact by ShortComplex.cokernelSequence_exact. The restriction-stalk comparison makes the stalk of G' zero at every point outside Z'.

source.place: Tag 01YD, lemma-prepare-filter-support, proof: restriction of I^n F to X minus Z'; with Schemes Tag 01I8 and Modules Tag 01CE. Read online at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01YD.

proof.text: Outside Z the stalk inclusion of K is surjective, so its image ideal is top. The ideal-power quotient stalk formula identifies the cokernel stalk with F_x/F_x, hence it is a singleton. At exponent zero apply the product quotient formula directly to the identity inclusion of the unit sheaf. Package these two support bounds with coherence and short exactness.
